nary_nodes.label: Drought conditions worsen across Europe
evidence: Drought conditions have worsened across Central and Western Europe since the start of the summer with southern England, northern Italy and parts of Central Europe among the hardest-hit areas, according to the Global Drought Observatory.

nary_nodes.label: Global Drought Observatory reports worsening drought
evidence: Drought conditions have worsened across Central and Western Europe since the start of the summer with southern England, northern Italy and parts of Central Europe among the hardest-hit areas, according to the Global Drought Observatory.

nary_nodes.label: Combined Drought Indicator reports Europe's drought area
evidence: About half of Europe’s land area is experiencing drought with 9 percent reaching the alert level, including southern Germany, Hungary, Romania, Austria, the Czech Republic and Slovakia, according to the Combined Drought Indicator for mid-July.

nary_nodes.label: JRC reports rivers at record-low levels
evidence: On Wednesday, the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre said the Loire, Po, Rhine and Danube rivers had reached record-low levels after continued hotter and drier conditions.

nary_nodes.label: Al Jazeera analyzes satellite imagery
evidence: Al Jazeera’s Open Source Unit analysed satellite imagery showing signs of worsening drought, including retreating water in major rivers, declining soil moisture and the yellowing of green spaces in several cities.

nary_nodes.label: Loire River channel changes visible in satellite images
evidence: A time-series comparison of satellite images of the Loire River near the French city of Saumur shows a clear change in the shape of the river channel during August from 2023 to 2026.
In images from previous years, larger portions of the channel appear to be covered by water while later comparisons reveal wider islands and larger sandy and gravelly areas within the river.

In an image captured on August 8 this year, substantially larger exposed areas can be seen within the channel compared with the previous images, coinciding with surrounding agricultural areas turning brown and pale.

nary_nodes.label: JRC reports Loire at record-low levels
evidence: These visual changes are consistent with the broader picture documented by the Joint Research Centre, which said the Loire had reached record-low levels in August.

nary_nodes.label: Garonne River area vegetation color changes
evidence: Near Moissac in southwestern France, a satellite comparison from May 21 to August 1 shows a considerable change in the colour of farm areas and vegetation surrounding the Garonne River.
In the May image, large areas of fields and vegetation appear in shades of green while the August image shows larger areas in brown and pale shades.

nary_nodes.label: Garonne basin experiences hydrological stress
evidence: These conditions have occurred during documented hydrological stress in the Garonne basin.

nary_nodes.label: Garonne authority begins early operation
evidence: In early July, the Garonne River management authority began an early operation to support river levels, describing it as the earliest such intervention since the system was introduced in 1993 after river flows near Toulouse approached record-low levels for that time of year.

nary_nodes.label: Rhine River channel exposed areas expand
evidence: In Germany, comparisons of satellite images taken near Kaub show an expansion of exposed sandy and gravelly areas within the Rhine River channel from May 1 to July 29.

In the May image, the channel appears filled with water while the late July image reveals larger exposed areas within the river and along its banks, accompanied by a clear change in the colour of surrounding vegetation and fields.

nary_nodes.label: Rhine water levels disrupt shipping
evidence: Rhine water levels in Germany have reached record lows, causing disruptions to shipping.

On Wednesday, the Reuters news agency reported that falling water levels had reached unprecedented levels and brought shipping traffic to a halt at a bottleneck on the river with some vessels becoming stranded.

nary_nodes.label: Reuters reports Rhine water levels halt shipping
evidence: On Wednesday, the Reuters news agency reported that falling water levels had reached unprecedented levels and brought shipping traffic to a halt at a bottleneck on the river with some vessels becoming stranded.

nary_nodes.label: German transport sector warns of navigation impossibility
evidence: Earlier, Germany’s inland waterway transport sector warned that the severe decline near Kaub could make commercial and tourist navigation impossible on parts of the river.

nary_nodes.label: Po River channel changes visible in satellite images
evidence: In Italy, images of the Po River near Boretto in the Emilia-Romagna region show changes in the extent of water and exposed areas during August in 2023 and 2026.
The 2023 image shows a larger water-covered area in parts of the channel while the 2026 image shows sandy and gravelly areas.

nary_nodes.label: JRC reports Po basin hydrological stress
evidence: This coincides with the Joint Research Centre’s report that the Po basin is experiencing severe hydrological stress while parts of Italy are facing pressure on water use for irrigation and energy production.

nary_nodes.label: Danube experiences water level declines
evidence: The impact of falling water levels is also visible on the Danube, which has experienced declines along several sections in Hungary and Romania.

nary_nodes.label: JRC reports reduced Danube flows impact
evidence: The Joint Research Centre said reduced Danube flows are putting pressure on navigation, water supplies and agricultural activity as well as the energy sector.

nary_nodes.label: Vegetation vitality declines in London
evidence: In England, satellite imagery captured visible changes across large areas of London, including Hyde Park, and the area around Stonehenge, where vegetation vitality has declined significantly.

nary_nodes.label: England records driest July since 1836
evidence: England recorded just 6.5mm (a quarter of an inch) of rainfall in July, equivalent to 10 percent of the long-term average, making it the driest July since records began in 1836.

nary_nodes.label: UK Environment Agency declares drought in England
evidence: On Tuesday, the United Kingdom’s Environment Agency announced that 71.3 percent of England was officially in drought, including all areas of Greater London, while reservoir storage had fallen to 69 percent.

nary_nodes.label: Vegetation vitality declines in Vienna
evidence: Satellite images of parks in the Austrian capital, Vienna, show changes in grass colour and water availability and the effects of extreme heat.
High-resolution satellite imagery from SkySat shows a striking visual change in the vitality of vegetation at Auer-Welsbach Park in Vienna between the summers of 2025 and 2026.

In an image captured on July 22, 2025, the park appears to have dark-green grassy areas complemented by lush tree cover. By contrast, the image captured on July 28, 2026, shows extensive yellowing and a severe decline in greenery, with most of the park’s open grassy areas turning brown and pale.

nary_nodes.label: Monitoring centres expect dry conditions to continue
evidence: European monitoring centres expect dry conditions to continue through September.

nary_nodes.label: River flows near Toulouse approached record-low levels
evidence: river flows near Toulouse approached record-low levels for that time of year.

nary_nodes.label: Vessels operating with lighter loads
evidence: Recent data also showed that vessels were operating with much lighter loads than usual because of reduced available draft.

evidence: the Po basin is experiencing severe hydrological stress

nary_nodes.label: Parts of Italy facing pressure on water use
evidence: parts of Italy are facing pressure on water use for irrigation and energy production.
